bug.title: The OCI bundle omits the /dev and /sys mounts gVisor needs to boot, so every GVisorSandbox run fails with runsc exit 128 before the signal runs
bug.symptoms: orchestrator._oci_bundle.build_bundle writes a config.json whose mounts are exactly /proc, a tmpfs /tmp, and the bind-mounted child. Running that bundle under the real runsc fails: `runsc --rootless --network=none --root STATE run --bundle BUNDLE ID` exits 128 with "cannot create sandbox: cannot read client sync file: waiting for sandbox to start: EOF", before the child executes. GVisorSandbox.run then reports fail_class crash, "the child exited (code 128) without writing a result envelope", for every signal, benign or hostile. A bundle generated by `runsc spec` (whose mounts are /proc, /dev, /sys) over the same runtime root runs the same interpreter to completion. The difference is the two missing virtual filesystems: gVisor's sandbox needs /dev (at least /dev/null, /dev/urandom) and /sys to boot. The unit tests pass because they drive a fake runsc and never boot a real sandbox.
bug.reproduction_steps: Build a bundle with build_bundle over a provisioned runtime root and run it under a real runsc in rootless mode. runsc exits 128 at sandbox creation. Generate a bundle with `runsc spec` over the same root, point its process at the same interpreter, and it exits 0.
bug.expected: - The bundle declares, besides /proc, the tmpfs /tmp and the child bind, two gVisor-virtualized filesystems with no host source: /dev (type "tmpfs" or "dev"/"devtmpfs" as gVisor accepts, options nosuid/strictatime/mode=0755/size=64k or the runsc-spec defaults) and /sys (type "sysfs", options nosuid/noexec/nodev/ro). Neither has a host path as source, so the "no host data mount" guarantee is unchanged: these are gVisor's own virtual devices and sysfs, not the host's. - A bundle built by build_bundle boots under the real runsc and the child writes its result envelope. The benign signal scores, and two runs are byte-identical. - validate_mounts accepts exactly the five destinations /proc, /dev, /sys, /tmp and the child bind, and still refuses any sixth mount, any wrong destination, and any bind whose source is under a lake root. - The lake-root refusals, the read-only root, the empty network namespace, the user 65534, the cgroup limits and JSON determinism are all unchanged. - A test marked to run only when runsc is on PATH and NULLIUS_GVISOR_RUNTIME_ROOT is set boots a real container from the generated bundle and asserts the child runs; it is skipped, with a reason, otherwise. The pure (fake-runsc) tests keep asserting the mount set, now five destinations.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/orchestrator/src/orchestrator/_oci_bundle.py builds mounts as only proc, tmpfs /tmp and the child bind. additions_spec_gvisor_executor.xml feature 4 said "mounts are only proc, a 64 MiB tmpfs at /tmp, and child_path bound read-only", which is too few: gVisor cannot start a sandbox without /dev and /sys.
bug.constraints: /dev and /sys are added as source-less gVisor-virtual filesystems, never host binds No test opens a network connection or reads a real credential; the real-runsc test skips when runsc is absent No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
